observed_title: A stochastic Carleson embedding theorem with constant e and the vector of Riesz transforms

read_ranges.scope: 全文逐页阅读：随机Carleson定理及Bellman/Itô证明，Gundy–Varopoulos半空间表示与配对引理证明，Riesz向量推论、适用边界、AI披露及参考文献

topic_relevance.I04: direct（随机占用/Carleson嵌入）：主定理是连续时间条件 Carleson 过程下，特定正交等变连续鞅系统的常数 e 嵌入；其半空间应用通过占用公式控制 Poisson 与 Riesz 向量。主题名中 LlogL 部分不由本文给出，须另找来源。

definitions.name: orthogonal/equivariant driver
definitions.statement: 连续平方可积鞅 X^0,…,X^n，满足 〈X^k,X^ℓ〉=0(k≠ℓ)，〈X^k〉=〈X^0〉。定义 u^0= u^0_0+Σ∫a^k dX^k，u^k=u^k_0+∫a^k dX^0−∫a^0 dX^k。

definitions.name: conditional Carleson occupancy condition (C)
definitions.statement: α≥0 progressive，M_t=E[∫_t^∞ α_s ds|F_t]≤1 a.s.；令 N_t=E[∫_0^∞α_s ds|F_t]，再假设 N 可表示为 N_0+Σ∫m^k dX^k。

definitions.name: Bellman state domain and function
definitions.statement: F_t=E[Σ_k|u^k_∞|²|F_t]，状态域 D={0≤M≤1, Σ_k (u^k)²≤F}；B(u,M,F)=eF−e^{1−M}Σ_k u_k²，故 0≤B≤eF。

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.1 (stochastic Carleson embedding, constant e)
assumptions: Usual conditions on the filtered probability space; fixed n≥1.
Continuous square-integrable martingales X⁰,…,Xⁿ are pairwise orthogonal and have equal quadratic variations.
The u^k processes have generalized Cauchy–Riemann integral form (2.2)–(2.3), with square-integrable integrands and L² terminal values.
α≥0 progressive and its conditional tail mass M_t=E[∫_t^∞α_s ds|F_t]≤1 a.s.
The closed martingale N associated with total α-mass lies in the stable subspace of the X^k with square-integrable progressive coefficients.
proof_steps: Define F_t as conditional terminal energy; Jensen puts (u_t,M_t,F_t) in D and the Bellman function is nonnegative and bounded by eF.
Apply multidimensional Itô to the continuous part e^{1−M_t}Σ(u_t^k)², keeping the Doob–Meyer drift of M separate because F_t need not be continuous.
Use orthogonality/equivariance to write all brackets explicitly; the finite variation remainder is ∫e^{1−M_s}Q_s d〈X⁰〉_s.
Rewrite Q as a sum of nonnegative squares using a Lagrange identity. The only dimension term is 2(n−1)(a⁰)², nonnegative for n≥1.
Take expectations, use e^{1−M}≥1 and B≥0, let t→∞, and use B≤eF to obtain the constant e.
gaps: The bound requires the strong structural martingale representation assumption for N; generic Carleson measures need not satisfy it.
No LlogL input or endpoint Orlicz variant is established in this paper.
The optimality of e is not claimed.
theorem_cards.proof_verification: full_text_read; assumptions/theorem visually checked on PDF p.3 and square decomposition/conclusion on pp.6–7; proof read but not independently re-proved.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.1 (Riesz-vector upper-half-space consequence)
assumptions: f is Schwartz on R^n; φ smooth on R^{n+1}_+ with Δφ≥0.
The integral on the left of (3.2) is finite.
Along background-radiation Brownian motion, α_s=Δφ(B_s) satisfies (C) and its closed martingale has representation (2.4) in the coordinate process filtration.
proof_steps: Use the background-radiation occupation formula (density 2y) to represent the left side as a stopped-path occupation integral.

For each k, prove an occupation pairing identity between the Gundy–Varopoulos martingale transform and the Poisson extension P_yR_kf by Green potential, stochastic Fubini, divergence theorem and ∂_yP_yR_kf=∂_{x_k}P_yf.
The pairing yields an L² occupation comparison; it does not assert equality of the two processes. For n=1 equality holds; for n≥2 it is generally strict.
Add the k estimates, identify the conditional Carleson density α=Δφ(B), and apply Theorem 2.1.
gaps: The setup assumes the Gundy–Varopoulos representation and the Carleson condition rather than deriving them for every φ.
For n≥2 only one Cauchy–Riemann derivative identity per Riesz component is used; the full gradient identity is false.
theorem_cards.proof_verification: full_text_read; main formula and assumptions visually checked on PDF p.8, occupation/combination step on p.13; proof read, not independently re-proved.

theorem_cards.label: Lemma 3.3 (occupation pairing identity)
assumptions: g∈C_c^∞(R^{n+1}_+); f is Schwartz; background-radiation setup as in Section 3.
proof_steps: Represent ∫_r^τg(B_s)ds using Dirichlet Green potential U.
Apply stochastic Fubini and martingale representation to convert the left occupation pairing to 2∫ y V·∇U.
Integrate by parts on a truncated half-ball; show hemispherical boundary flux vanishes using decay of U,V.
Apply Green identity to the right pairing and reduce to −2∫U∂_yv.
Use the Fourier identity ∂_yv=∂_{x_k}u to identify both pairings.
gaps: Proof invokes decay estimates for Schwartz data and limiting arguments; not independently checked.
Identity is an occupation pairing against position functions, not a process equality or conditional expectation identity.
theorem_cards.proof_verification: full_text_read; the pairing identity and final application visually checked on PDF pp.9–13; proof read, not independently re-proved.

constant_dependence.explicit: The main stochastic embedding has the explicit multiplicative constant e, independent of n.
constant_dependence.dependence: The algebraic nonnegativity uses n≥1; no dimension factor is lost in the Riesz-vector application.

endpoint_limits.time: Continuous-time and infinite-horizon formulation; passage to t→∞ uses nonnegative integrand and B bounded by eF.
endpoint_limits.martingale_structure: The driving martingales must be continuous, orthogonal, and have equal bracket; α-associated closed martingale must be representable in their stable subspace.
endpoint_limits.geometry: For n=1 the Riesz/Hilbert-transform comparison is equality; for n≥2 only an occupation inequality, generally strict.
endpoint_limits.missing_endpoint: No LlogL endpoint, weak-type extension, arbitrary optional projection, or generic stochastic process occupancy theorem is stated.

reusable_methods.method: Bellman–Itô square completion for a vector Carleson embedding
reusable_methods.transfer: For a candidate filtered occupancy problem, define a nonnegative conditional mass M and terminal energy F, then prove a state-domain inequality and calculate the full bracket quadratic form. Before using the constant e, verify all cross-bracket cancellation, equal bracket assumptions, and nonnegative square decomposition in the target system.
reusable_methods.limit: Here the generalized CR system and stable-subspace representation are essential; no automatic transfer to merely orthogonal increments.

reusable_methods.method: Occupation pairing can replace false process identity
reusable_methods.transfer: When stochastic-transform and analytic extension processes are not pathwise equal, test against compactly supported functions of the state and prove an occupation pairing by Green potentials and integration by parts; then use polarization/square expansion to get the L² comparison.
reusable_methods.limit: The pairing is specific to the Gundy–Varopoulos Brownian half-space representation and decay assumptions.
